narr: Numerous showers and thunderstorms affected southern Middle Tennessee during the early morning hours of March 31, 2021. Thunderstorms repeatedly moved across Wayne, Lawrence, and Giles Counties for many hours, causing widespread flash flooding.
ev: Westpoint Road at Waterloo Road was flooded and closed.
Henryville Road was flooded and closed. Most low water bridges across northern Lawrence County were flooded and impassable.
The roadways was washed out at 42 Waterfork Road. Numerous other roads were flooded across the county.
Widespread flash flooding was reported across northern Lawrence County. Long Road between Henryville Road and Cross Road was washed out.
Flood waters submerged the Helton Street bridge near Waynesboro Elementary School.
Swift water rescue was conducted from a vehicle trapped on the Brace Road bridge near Walker Road.
The northbound lane of Highway 240 was flooded near the Henryville Fire Department.
Several roads were flooded across the county including Highway 31N, Highway 129, Factory Creek Road, Old Campbellsville Road, and Pigeon Roost Road.
A vehicle was trapped in flood waters on Highway 240 near Barnesville Road. Occupant escaped safely.
Highway 240 at Henryville Road was closed due to high water.
Johnson Branch Road near Highway 64 was flooded and impassable.

Numerous additional roads were flooded and impassable across the county. These roads included Old Highway 64 in Frankewing, Minnow Branch Road, Gunter Smith Road, Robertson Hollow Road, Big Dry Creek Road, Little Dry Creek Road, Weakly Creek Road, Home Hill Road, Thomas Road, Kerr Hill Road, Milky Way Road, Locke Road, Annie Wade Road, Dog Branch Road, Mack Branch Road, Owl Hollow Road, Highway 31A, Vales Mill Road, and Greene Valley Road.
Highway 64 was covered by flood waters near the Philadelphia Baptist Church at 2254 Savannah Highway.
Several homes were surrounded by flood waters on Sunny Acres Drive.
Gwinn Road was flooded and closed.
